cases.name: array.geometry_vs_v2_recording
cases.against: tower x, y and base z, the room and 2T of docs/viewer-mockup/replay.json (the v2 recording); largest difference

cases.name: engine.cached_sum_equals_cold_run
cases.against: superposition after a drag of one body and back, summed from kept contributions, against a cold run of the same scene; values of any channel that differ, to the bit

cases.name: engine.replay
cases.against: a session replayed from its journal, and from its journal saved as JSON; replays whose state digest differs

cases.name: forward.precision_far
cases.against: the oscillation anchor and a tower 1.36 m from it, both moved by (10000.3, -7000.7, 300.1) m, read the same series as at the origin; largest difference as a fraction of the peak

cases.name: forward.quadrature_order
cases.against: Gauss-Legendre with 3 nodes a panel converges as h^6: the oscillation anchor's lower-interferometer phase at panels of T/2, T/4, T/8, T/16 against 12 nodes on T/64 (floor off, so the pieces are the two halves)

cases.name: forward.quadrature_on_the_anchors
cases.against: the engine's rule (Gauss, 6 nodes, 0.1 s panels) against 12 nodes on 0.025 s panels, on a static mass and the two published anchors; largest difference as a fraction of each series' peak

cases.name: forward.audited_read_close_pass
cases.against: 10 kg passing 0.5 m from a tower at 2.5 m/s, read until two successive rules agree to 1e-10 rad, against 12 nodes on 1.6 ms panels; largest error over 25 shots and both interferometers

cases.name: forward.v1_anchor_fixture
cases.against: v1's outputs on the three anchors and on the oscillation read by the five towers, frozen in oracle/fixtures/v1 (the oracle tier checks them against v1 itself); engine set to v1's conventions; largest difference as a fraction of each series' peak

cases.name: maths.perspective_divide
cases.against: the CPU matrix Mat4::perspective only, not the renderer: a point ten times further away projects ten times nearer the axis

cases.name: nulls.finite_floor_edge
cases.against: a concrete disc 1 m thick under a tower on its axis, radius 400 m to 6.4 km: the gradiometer's reading as a fraction of what one interferometer reads from the infinite slab; it falls as 1/R, the edge's uniform gradient, towards the slab's zero

cases.name: nulls.infinite_floor
cases.against: an infinite uniform slab (and the half-space) gives uniform g: gradiometer values, over five towers at different heights and six shots, that are not exactly zero

cases.name: nulls.void
cases.against: the void: the array and nothing else; values of any channel of any tower's any shot that are not exactly zero

cases.name: render.gpu_projection
cases.against: the f64 camera's projection of a point on each tower; distance to the centre of the nearest pixel of that tower's colour, worst over five towers and four views. The measure resolves no finer than half a pixel's diagonal, 0.71 px

cases.name: render.gpu_perspective_ratio
cases.against: the ratio of the on-screen heights of a near and a far tower, as the f64 camera predicts it

cases.name: render.gpu_determinism
cases.against: the same frame drawn twice, and by a second renderer on the same device; bytes that differ

cases.name: render.gpu_local_frame_at_10_km
cases.against: end to end on the GPU: the infinite-floor scene moved by (10000, -7000, 300) m, camera and all, against the same scene at the origin; bytes of the picture that differ

cases.name: render.local_frame_at_10_km
cases.against: CPU geometry only: the vertices of the same scene built at the world origin, each relative to its own target

cases.name: scenes.flash

cases.name: scenes.precision_far
cases.against: precision-far: the scene 10 km from the origin against the same scene at the origin, all five towers; largest difference as a fraction of each tower's peak

cases.name: scenes.switch_on
cases.against: switch-on: the shot in flight when the mass appears reads the always-there mass's integral from the switch to the readout (12 nodes on 2 ms panels); shots before read nothing, shots after read all of it; largest difference as a fraction of the full reading

cases.name: scenes.time_reversal
cases.against: time-reversal: with the launch that closes the arms at 2T (u0 = gT - v_kick/2), a pass played backwards reads the forward pass's series in reverse; largest difference over five towers as a fraction of the peak

cases.name: scenes.ring_orbit
cases.against: ring-orbit: a mass circling the centre tower at fixed radius and height reads the same every shot; largest departure from the mean as a fraction of it

cases.name: scenes.mirror_pair
cases.against: mirror-pair: towers 2 and 3 swap their readings of the two bodies, and towers 1, 4 and 5 read the same from each; values that differ, to the bit

cases.name: scenes.superposition
cases.against: superposition: A alone, B alone, A + B; values of any channel, tower and shot where the reading of both is not the sum of the two, to the bit

cases.name: spec.json_round_trip
cases.against: a spec of awkward numbers written to JSON and read back; numbers whose bits differ

cases.name: spec.ron_round_trip
cases.against: a spec of awkward numbers written to RON and read back; numbers whose bits differ

cases.name: spectrum.lomb_scargle_equals_fft
cases.against: on a uniform, gap-free grid Lomb-Scargle (Scargle's tau, mean taken off, times dt_eff) is the classical periodogram: 2000 shots of a comb, a tone and noise, every bin below Nyquist; largest relative difference
